problem: Narváez's fleet landed c. 22 April, but Cortés did not learn of it in Tenochtitlan that day; news reached him days to weeks later. The entry is about Cortés receiving the news, so a single-day date is wrong.

problem: The detail that the disease began 'in the house where he lodged' is Gómara's and Motolinía's anecdote (one house), not attested for Díaz in McCaa's Table 2; the source_note also carries a compiler remark.

fix.digest: Díaz recalled that Narváez brought a Black man who was full of smallpox, and that the illness struck the people of Cempoala and spread from there, with great mortality. He added that the people of that land had never had the disease before, and that it then spread through New Spain. He wrote this forty years later, already knowing what followed.
fix.source_note: Historia verdadera, Cempoala episode (Díaz I, 373 in the edition cited by McCaa, https://users.pop.umn.edu/~rmccaa/vircatas/vir6.htm; McCaa Table 2, https://users.pop.umn.edu/~rmccaa/vircatas/virtab2.htm). Digest only.

problem: The phrase 'there has Not so much as One miscarried' is from a William Cooper sidebar, not the Gazette letter 'probably by Rev. Cotton Mather'. That letter says more than threescore had been inoculated and that one gentlewoman, already infected naturally, died, so 'not one had died' misstates it.

fix.digest: A letter in the Gazette, probably by Mather, reported that more than threescore people had undergone inoculation and that only one had died, a woman already infected with natural smallpox. He set this beside the burials in the town. Deaths after inoculation were recorded later in the epidemic.
fix.headline: More than threescore inoculated
fix.source_note: NHC selections (spelling and punctuation modernised by NHC), Boston Gazette 23–30 Oct 1721, 'A Faithful Account', attributed by NHC to Mather as probable author.

problem: The James Lind Library says Boylston presented his book to the Royal Society meeting chaired by Newton in 1726, at about the same time Jurin published his figures. It does not say Jurin presented his figures at that meeting.

fix.digest: Jurin's accumulated English figures counted 13 deaths among 624 inoculated against 2,848 deaths among 22,151 natural cases. At about the same time Boylston presented his Boston book to a Royal Society meeting chaired by Sir Isaac Newton, and the two sets of figures could be set side by side.
fix.headline: England's cumulative figures, and Boylston before Newton

fix.headline: A pseudonymous letter attacks the experiment
fix.digest: Under the pseudonym 'W. Philanthroper' (as the NHC selections give it), Douglass told readers that inoculation came from Thessaly by way of Constantinople, that it was unproven, and that Boylston was acting rashly by spreading the infection. He called on the magistrates to act. In 1722 he referred back to this letter in Campbell's paper as a mere caution.
